Analysis of the post-retrofit data clearly illustrates these improvements; although electrification was not a major part of these improvements, fuel oil use overall was lowered (Figure 3). 2017 Annual Energy Usage (kBtu) 97,583 522,651 Electricity Consumption Fuel Oil Consumption (modeled) 2024 Energy Demand (kBtu) 57,322 293,991 Electricity Consumption Fuel Oil Consumption Figure 3: The proportion of energy use did not change, but the overall consumption decreased by 47% once the retrofits were in place. Observed monthly fuel oil usage during the post-retrofit period (2024–25) consistently trended lower than historical consumption patterns from pre-retrofit and baseline years (2016–17; Figure 4). Figure 4: Monthly fuel oil usage (gallons) for heating and heating degree days (HDD) for years 2017 (pre-retrofit), and 2024 (post-retrofit). Fuel oil consumption is represented by columns (primary y-axis), while HDD values are shown as dashed lines (secondary y-axis). Data are presented monthly to illustrate seasonal variation and year-to-year differences in fuel oil use and HDD. EUI was used to evaluate overall building energy performance (i.e., fuel oil and electricity) and showed a substantial reduction of approximately 47% compared to the baseline established in 2016 (Figure 5). The observed savings could translate into financial benefits for the community, enabling the possibility of further reinvestment into infrastructure. The marked decrease, especially in winter, underscores the effectiveness of the implemented retrofits in this heating-dominated setting. LED substitution, boiler and hydronic distribution system improvements, and the installation and explanation of programmable thermostats each contributed to the overall reduction in energy use.
